name: Application Shell
purpose: Define the persistent structural frame that organizes the main Aurora application environment, separating global application context, navigation and product workspace.
problem: Without a consistent application shell, products can recreate global navigation, mix global and local responsibilities, duplicate headers and alter workspace hierarchy in inconsistent ways.
whenToUse: Authenticated Aurora application workspaces that require global navigation.
Product or module experiences that live inside the main Aurora environment.
Operational workspaces, dashboards, listings, maps and monitoring experiences that share the global application frame.
whenNotToUse: Public pages, isolated authentication experiences, landing pages or standalone experiences are not yet validated uses of this pattern.

evidence.observation: Header/Hero, Navigation/Global and Workspace surface remain present while a contextual notification panel opens.
Header/Hero, Navigation/Global, Breadcrumbs and a product workspace compose an ERP operational screen.
The same shell structure is preserved when the workspace content is an Empty State.
The same application shell is reused for an operational videowall workspace.

anatomy.purpose: Provide persistent global application context and global actions.
Provide navigation between major products, tools or application areas.
Host the active product or feature experience.
Provide contextual orientation such as breadcrumbs inside the workspace context.

compositionRules: Global navigation must remain outside feature content.
The global header belongs to the shell and must not be recreated inside individual feature screens.
Breadcrumbs belong to workspace context and must not replace global or product navigation.
The workspace may contain dashboards, tables, maps, videowalls, empty states and contextual panels without changing the shell hierarchy.
Contextual overlays may coexist with the shell when the underlying application context must remain available.
Feature-specific navigation must remain inside the product or workspace context.

states.name: empty
states.reason: Handled by the active workspace or feature.

contentRules: Global navigation labels and workspace titles must preserve distinct responsibilities.
Breadcrumb content should communicate workspace context rather than act as primary application navigation.
constraints: Do not recreate global navigation inside feature content.
Do not duplicate the global header inside the workspace.
Do not use breadcrumbs as a replacement for global navigation.
Keep feature-specific navigation inside the workspace context.
Do not change the shell hierarchy to accommodate a local feature without an explicit system-level decision.
Reuse approved Aurora navigation contracts before introducing custom navigation.
antiPatterns: Creating a second global navigation inside the workspace.
Duplicating the global header within product content.
Using breadcrumbs as primary application navigation.
Allowing an individual feature to redefine the global shell hierarchy.
Creating a custom shell per module without an explicit architecture decision.

must: Preserve the hierarchy Global Header -> Global Navigation -> Workspace.
Keep product-specific content inside the workspace.
Reuse Breadcrumbs when contextual navigation is required.
Preserve global navigation outside feature composition.
should: Use Application Shell as the default structure for authenticated Aurora application workspaces.
Preserve user context when feature content changes.
Compose feature-specific patterns inside the workspace.
mustNot: Invent a new application shell when this pattern satisfies the requirement.
Mix global navigation and product navigation responsibilities.
Invent keyboard, persistence or routing behavior.
Replace Aurora components with visually similar custom structures.

openQuestions: Is Header/Hero formally part of Aurora Core Components?
How should the shell behave on mobile?
What determines expanded versus collapsed state?
What is the keyboard navigation model?
What landmarks and ARIA structure should engineering use?
How does product-level navigation interact with Global Navigation?
Is Breadcrumb mandatory for every product screen or contextual?
Are global overlays allowed to cover navigation?
What permission rules affect global navigation visibility?
